To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## Preliminary point: the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" preamble

The Seller's cover note says these positions were "settled at principal level" and "are not intended to be re-opened." It also says caps, baskets and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "standard and widely accepted."

- **This is advocacy, not agreement.** Nothing in the papers evidences a principal-level settlement, such as a signed term sheet or heads of terms.
- **Confirm internally** whether Wattlebridge principals agreed any of these points before conceding anything on that basis.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its "addressed" claims.** It confirms that Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment evidence and the DD-006 investigation are all outstanding.

I have reviewed every point on its merits below.

**Staleness:** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. It is now 5 November 2026. Every open matter needs a bring-down and an updated disclosure before signing.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)

- **Seller:** Aggregate cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A higher general cap. Open at 50% (AUD 12m) and be prepared to land around 30–35%.
  - The cap should apply only to general Warranty Claims.
  - Fundamental/title warranties, tax and specific indemnities should be capped at 100% of price, or uncapped for fraud.
  - If W&I insurance is used, structure the Seller cap around the retention, with a Seller backstop for known and excluded matters.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** 20% is low given the cluster of known, unresolved risks (30% customer concentration, IP chain gap, privacy incident). Those risks must sit outside this cap in any event.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)

- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25k per claim. A AUD 250k basket (~1%) that operates as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - De minimis of AUD 10–15k, with related or recurring claims aggregated.
  - A **tipping** basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar) at around 0.5% (AUD 120k).
  - No de minimis or basket for fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** A deductible basket plus a no-aggregation de minimis could wipe out recovery on a series of mid-sized SaaS issues, such as customer credits or privacy remediation.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)

- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general claims. Seller also proposes that every limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two full audit cycles post-Completion.
  - Tax: the relevant ATO amendment period plus 6 months (practically 5–7 years).
  - Title/fundamental: 7 years, or the NSW limitation period (6 years for contract, 12 years if executed as a deed).
  - Specific indemnities: running until the underlying matter is finally resolved.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** 18 months may expire before the Bluefen renewal, privacy regulator or ATO consequences surface.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime

- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Capacity, authority, title, issued capital and no-encumbrance warranties as fundamental warranties.
  - Capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis or basket, no disclosure against them, and the long time limit above.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. Capping that at AUD 4.8m is not "administrative simplicity."

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)

- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An express carve-out stating that no limitation, exclusive remedy, non-reliance or disclosure provision applies to claims arising from fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or advisers.
  - Express preservation of statutory claims that cannot lawfully be excluded, including the misleading or deceptive conduct prohibition under the Australian Consumer Law.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert a carve-out.** A seller should never be able to cap or exclude liability for its own fraud. The non-reliance clause could otherwise be used to resist a misrepresentation claim.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)

- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and all public records. DL 1.4 also contains a blanket non-admission.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Warranties qualified only by matters **fairly disclosed** in the Disclosure Letter, with sufficient detail to identify the nature, scope and quantum of the matter.
  - No general data room disclosure. If the data room is referenced at all, it should be a fixed, indexed copy on USB, limited to specific cross-referenced documents.
  - Public records limited to named searches (ASIC, PPSR, court) as at a specified date.
  - No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax indemnity or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** General disclosure converts the warranties into a "find it yourself" exercise and undermines warranty protection and any W&I cover.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)

- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An express statement that warranty claims are not affected by any knowledge of the Buyer or its advisers, actual, constructive or imputed, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
  - At most, as a fallback: actual knowledge of named Buyer deal team individuals, and never against specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge is effectively constructive knowledge. It would neutralise the warranties, and the specific indemnities exist precisely because the Buyer knows of these issues.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)

- **Seller:** "Addressed." Reasonable endeavours, with the condition satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. DL 2 confirms that **no final consent or evidence of satisfaction of the cl 11.3 conditions** has been provided.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - A condition precedent requiring an unconditional written consent from Bluefen under DD-002 cl 11.2, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - Evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, and confirmation of no termination or adverse amendment.
  - Waivable by the Buyer only.
  - Seller to use best endeavours, with a long-stop date.
  - Fallback: a price adjustment, earn-out or retention tied to Bluefen continuity, or a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates within 12 months by reason of the change of control.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "addressed" characterisation; insert a hard condition precedent.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, or about 30% of FY26 revenue. A bare consent that ignores the cl 11.3 conditions may not be effective.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)

- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 confirms the ~AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid with no discharge of security, and the facility has a change-control clause at cl 8.1.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The outstanding balance treated as Debt, deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark at Completion under a payout letter.
  - The following delivered **at** Completion as a completion deliverable: a deed of release, PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge within a set number of days), and a release of any share mortgage or guarantee.
  - The payout amount should include break costs and fees.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A post-Completion release breaches the debt-free basis. The cl 8.1 change of control may trigger a default at Completion, and the Buyer would own a company subject to AUD 3.2m of security with no leverage.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)

- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price. On-costs include superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - The bonuses paid through Company payroll at Completion, funded from the price.
  - A specific indemnity covering any shortfall, plus a warranty that no other change-of-control payments exist.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the current funds flow.** The Company, not the Seller, is the legal obligor. Leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow shifts roughly AUD 420k plus on-costs onto the Buyer, contrary to debt-free/cash-free.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)

- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." DL 4 confirms:
  - Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until **every** SOW3 fee has cleared.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180k open.
  - There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Condition precedent or completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment, plus a confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consents from Ironquay.
  - If that cannot be delivered, a specific indemnity covering **all** losses arising from the Company not owning the SOW3 Project Materials. That includes re-engineering, licence fees and third-party claims, not just the AUD 180k.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, de minimis, basket and time limit, and be backed by an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee but a gap in the chain of title to IP that may be core to the product.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006)

- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." DL 6 states:
  - A download link to ~1,240 records was sent to an unintended external address.
  - Whether the file was accessed, the scope of the export, and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Immediate disclosure of the incident date, the investigation status, and whether an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act Part IIIC) was completed within the 30-day window. Given the 22 September disclosure date, that window has likely passed.
  - Any forensic report and any notifications made to the OAIC, customers or affected individuals.
  - A specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, and exposure under the statutory privacy tort. The indemnity should sit outside the general limitations.
  - A retention, and a pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and comply with the scheme.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "not material" characterisation; insert a specific indemnity and retention.** The Seller cannot call an un-scoped, un-assessed incident immaterial, and the NDB timing creates live regulatory exposure.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)

- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 describes them as "related," says they should be read together, and is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An explanation of why one arrangement was split into three equal renewals. Confirm whether this avoided an approval threshold or a conduct-of-business restriction.
  - Copies of the renewals, their terms, and their termination rights.
  - Confirmation of whether any are with a Seller-related party.
  - Seller to obtain Buyer consent for any further commitments.
  - Any non-ordinary-course or prepaid or accrued amounts treated as Debt or a price adjustment, or covered by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER; do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without evidence.** Three identical "related" renewals is a pattern consistent with threshold-splitting.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want the default reversed.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, with separate defined regimes for each of:
  1. Fundamental warranties
  2. Tax warranties and indemnity
  3. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Bluefen, Sandbar)
  4. Covenant and completion-obligation claims
  5. Fraud

  In addition, claims under categories 2–5 should not count towards the general cap or basket, and there should be an express no-double-recovery provision.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The Seller's default sweeps every specific indemnity under the 20% cap and 18-month limit, which would hollow out the protections negotiated for the known issues.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)

- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the Company share register. DL 10 concedes this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want the following independent checks:**
  - ASIC company extract and historical shareholding.
  - PPSR search against the Seller as grantor and against the shares, including any share mortgage to Riverlark.
  - Review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption rights.
  - Confirmation that no options, ESOP awards, convertible notes or SAFEs exist.
- **The Buyer should also require the following at Completion:**
  - Original share certificates or an indemnity for lost certificates.
  - Signed transfers.
  - Board minutes approving registration.
  - Waivers of pre-emption rights.
  - Releases of any share security.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER; verify independently and make title a fundamental warranty.** A register maintained by the Seller is self-certification, not proof of title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms

- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-one recovery, a cap of 100% of price, a time limit of the amendment period plus 6 months, and conduct-of-claims provisions. Tax warranties should cover payroll tax and superannuation, which links to SPA-N-010, as well as R&D incentive claims if relevant.
  - **IP:** Ownership, no-infringement, open-source compliance and data protection warranties with an elevated cap (for example 50%), a 36-month time limit, and the Ironquay and DD-006 matters carved out into specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled."** These terms are open, and the general regime is inappropriate for a SaaS target where IP and tax are core value drivers.

---

## Priority actions

1. **Reply to Seller counsel** that the package is not accepted as final, and attach the Buyer mark-up.
2. **Completion conditions and deliverables:** Bluefen consent, the Riverlark payout and release, and the Ironquay assignment.
3. **Funds flow corrections:** Riverlark payout, the bonuses plus on-costs, and any Sandbar adjustment.
4. **Information requests:** the DD-006 forensic and NDB status, the Sandbar contracts and rationale, the Ironquay payment evidence, the ASIC and PPSR searches, and an updated disclosure bring-down.
5. **W&I:** If W&I insurance is being considered, start underwriting now. Known matters (Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006) will be excluded, which reinforces the need for Seller-backed specific indemnities.

*These are recommended negotiating positions for the Buyer deal team and should be confirmed by NSW-qualified transaction counsel before being sent.*

- **Recommendation: REJECT the "addressed" characterisation; insert a hard condition precedent.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, or about 30% of FY26 revenue. A bare consent that ignores the cl 11.3 conditions may not be effective.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)

- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL 3 confirms the ~AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid with no discharge of security, and the facility has a change-control clause at cl 8.1.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The outstanding balance treated as Debt, deducted from the price and paid directly to Riverlark at Completion under a payout letter.
  - The following delivered **at** Completion as a completion deliverable: a deed of release, PPSR financing change statements (or an undertaking to lodge within a set number of days), and a release of any share mortgage or guarantee.
  - The payout amount should include break costs and fees.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** A post-Completion release breaches the debt-free basis. The cl 8.1 change of control may trigger a default at Completion, and the Buyer would own a company subject to AUD 3.2m of security with no leverage.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)

- **Seller:** AUD 420k of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter is silent on on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - The bonuses plus all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price. On-costs include superannuation guarantee, NSW payroll tax, PAYG withholding and workers' compensation.
  - The bonuses paid through Company payroll at Completion, funded from the price.
  - A specific indemnity covering any shortfall, plus a warranty that no other change-of-control payments exist.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the current funds flow.** The Company, not the Seller, is the legal obligor. Leaving the bonuses out of the funds flow shifts roughly AUD 420k plus on-costs onto the Buyer, contrary to debt-free/cash-free.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)

- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate." DL 4 confirms:
  - Under DD-004 cl 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until **every** SOW3 fee has cleared.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180k open.
  - There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Condition precedent or completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment, plus a confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consents from Ironquay.
  - If that cannot be delivered, a specific indemnity covering **all** losses arising from the Company not owning the SOW3 Project Materials. That includes re-engineering, licence fees and third-party claims, not just the AUD 180k.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap, de minimis, basket and time limit, and be backed by an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER.** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee but a gap in the chain of title to IP that may be core to the product.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006)

- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." DL 6 states:
  - A download link to ~1,240 records was sent to an unintended external address.
  - Whether the file was accessed, the scope of the export, and whether notification is required are all unknown.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - Immediate disclosure of the incident date, the investigation status, and whether an assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act Part IIIC) was completed within the 30-day window. Given the 22 September disclosure date, that window has likely passed.
  - Any forensic report and any notifications made to the OAIC, customers or affected individuals.
  - A specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident, including regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims and credits, and exposure under the statutory privacy tort. The indemnity should sit outside the general limitations.
  - A retention, and a pre-Completion covenant to complete the investigation and comply with the scheme.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "not material" characterisation; insert a specific indemnity and retention.** The Seller cannot call an un-scoped, un-assessed incident immaterial, and the NDB timing creates live regulatory exposure.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)

- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate) are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8 describes them as "related," says they should be read together, and is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer should want:**
  - An explanation of why one arrangement was split into three equal renewals. Confirm whether this avoided an approval threshold or a conduct-of-business restriction.
  - Copies of the renewals, their terms, and their termination rights.
  - Confirmation of whether any are with a Seller-related party.
  - Seller to obtain Buyer consent for any further commitments.
  - Any non-ordinary-course or prepaid or accrued amounts treated as Debt or a price adjustment, or covered by an indemnity.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER; do not accept the "ordinary course" characterisation without evidence.** Three identical "related" renewals is a pattern consistent with threshold-splitting.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation

- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer should want the default reversed.** Limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims, with separate defined regimes for each of:
  1. Fundamental warranties
  2. Tax warranties and indemnity
  3. Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Bluefen, Sandbar)
  4. Covenant and completion-obligation claims
  5. Fraud

  In addition, claims under categories 2–5 should not count towards the general cap or basket, and there should be an express no-double-recovery provision.
- **Recommendation: REJECT.** The Seller's default sweeps every specific indemnity under the 20% cap and 18-month limit, which would hollow out the protections negotiated for the known issues.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)

- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the Company share register. DL 10 concedes this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer should want the following independent checks:**
  - ASIC company extract and historical shareholding.
  - PPSR search against the Seller as grantor and against the shares, including any share mortgage to Riverlark.
  - Review of the constitution and any shareholders' agreement for pre-emption rights.
  - Confirmation that no options, ESOP awards, convertible notes or SAFEs exist.
- **The Buyer should also require the following at Completion:**
  - Original share certificates or an indemnity for lost certificates.
  - Signed transfers.
  - Board minutes approving registration.
  - Waivers of pre-emption rights.
  - Releases of any share security.
- **Recommendation: COUNTER; verify independently and make title a fundamental warranty.** A register maintained by the Seller is self-certification, not proof of title.

## SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms

- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, AUD 250k basket, 18 months).
- **Buyer should want:**
  - **Tax:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity, dollar-one recovery, a cap of 100% of price, a time limit of the amendment period plus 6 months, and conduct-of-claims provisions. Tax warranties should cover payroll tax and superannuation, which links to SPA-N-010, as well as R&D incentive claims if relevant.
  - **IP:** Ownership, no-infringement, open-source compliance and data protection warranties with an elevated cap (for example 50%), a 36-month time limit, and the Ironquay and DD-006 matters carved out into specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled."** These terms are open, and the general regime is inappropriate for a SaaS target where IP and tax are core value drivers.
